metadata.technology_specification: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) system
metadata.technology_reasoning: Triple Quadrupole LC–MS systems are the industry-standard analytical instruments for targeted quantification and confirmation in complex mixtures, widely adopted across pharmaceutical, environmental, food safety, and clinical testing sectors due to their high specificity and sensitivity offered by tandem mass spectrometry with triple quadrupole analyzers.

components.reasoning: Primary subsystem responsible for sample separation; procured as a distinct unit with its own fluidics, pumps, and injector system, universally part of LC–MS setups.
Essential component where analytes are ionized (commonly Electrospray Ionization - ESI or Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionization - APCI); must be separately sourced and integrated.
The first mass analyzer that selects precursor ions; a core element of triple quadrupole systems always present as a discrete component.
Central quadrupole used for collision-induced dissociation (CID) generating product ions; distinctive subassembly in triple quadrupole MS.
Analyzes product ions from the collision cell for quantification and confirmation; critical and always present as a separate mass filter.
Includes turbomolecular and roughing pumps maintaining required high vacuum conditions throughout MS; separate subsystem essential for proper instrument function.
Electron multiplier or similar detector converting ions to an electrical signal; integral to MS subsystem and usually modular.
Electronics and software modules for instrument control, data acquisition, and processing; distinct component usually procured or developed separately.
Structural framework holding components, including user interface panels and computer interface; standard as a separate module.
